researched_by: the council's own motorhome and oversize vehicle parking page, its town-by-town parking tariff pages, the 2025 alcohol PSPO and the council's PSPO index, the Traffic Penalty Tribunal traffic regulation order repository for the Isle of Wight, OnTheWight's reporting on the introduction of the overnight charge, and ONS postcode centroids via postcodes.io
policy_summary:
No aire, no motorhome bays, no waste point, no trial and no proposal - and yet the Isle of Wight is one of the easiest places in England to spend a legal night in a vehicle, because the council sells you the night for two pounds and never once mentions motorhomes when it does.

The island's regime has three parts. First, a published list of seventeen council car parks in Chale, Cowes, Newport, Ryde, Sandown, Seaview, Shanklin, St Helens, Ventnor and Yarmouth where motorhomes and oversize vehicles are directed to park, each with a postcode, a note on which bay or surface to use, whether there are toilets nearby, and a height-barrier column that reads 'No' at every single one. No council car park on the island excludes motor caravans by class. Ryde's tariff page goes further and lists Quay Road as taking 'Coach, HGV, Motorhomes, oversized vehicles' outright.

Second, an island-wide overnight charge. Every town tariff checked carries the same line - 'overnight charge (6pm - 8am) - GBP2.00' off-street, and 'overnight charge (6pm - 10am) - GBP2.00' on-street. It was introduced at GBP1 in 2019, applies to on-street and off-street alike, and has since doubled. A tourist multi-location permit covering most council pay and display, valid 24 hours a day, runs GBP20 for two days to GBP140 for fourteen; a separate oversize/coach permit runs GBP83.20 for four days to GBP145.60 for seven. Overnight parking is not tolerated here, it is a product.

Third, one prohibition, and it is on the act rather than the vehicle: 'You must not use your vehicle for cooking, sleeping, sanitary or any other purpose whilst in the car park.' That is the whole of the island's anti-sleeping law. It sits in the off-street parking places order regime (the Parking Places (Consolidation) Order No 3 2023, amended by Order No 4 2023) and applies to all vehicles, not to motorhomes specifically.

What is not there matters as much. The seven Public Spaces Protection Orders in force - East Cowes, Freshwater/Totland, Lake, Newport, Ryde, Sandown and Shanklin - are alcohol control orders made 5 July 2025 for three years, and none of them mentions camping, vehicles, caravans or overnight sleeping. No on-street order was found restricting bays to cars and motorcycles, no no-overnight-parking window, no motorhome-specific order, no consultation, no council report on campervan pressure. On an island where four ferry terminals (Ryde, Fishbourne, East Cowes, Yarmouth) dump arrivals in clusters and the south coast towns absorb them, the council has responded by charging two pounds and asking people not to sleep.
notes:
The direction of travel is monetisation, not prohibition, and the Isle of Wight is the clearest example of it in the dataset. Where BCP is drafting an experimental order to make the vehicle's presence the offence, and North Yorkshire and East Suffolk have already done it, the Isle of Wight has spent the same years raising the overnight charge from GBP1 to GBP2 and publishing a helpful table telling motorhomes where to go. Nothing found suggests that is about to change.

The enforcement reality follows from the drafting. A sleeping ban requires an officer to establish what is happening inside a vehicle; the council's other rule - 'the whole of the vehicle must be inside the marked bay' - requires only a look. That is the rule that actually catches motorhomes, and the forum evidence bears it out: a user reporting a ticket 'within five minutes' for minor overhang, and nobody reporting being woken. The seventeen-car-park list is in effect the council telling large vehicles which bays are long enough to avoid that PCN.

The unitary status produces an unresolved gap worth flagging. The 'no cooking, sleeping, sanitary' clause is a condition of the CAR PARK. The council also sells a GBP2 overnight ticket for on-street bays on Ryde Esplanade, Cowes Parade, Ventnor Esplanade and Yarmouth High Street, and no equivalent sleeping prohibition was found in any on-street order. If the clause does not travel onto the highway, an on-street bay is the better legal position - the opposite of the usual English pattern, where car parks are the tolerated place and the street is where the orders bite.

Two gaps in provision are geographically pointed. Of the four ferry ports, only Ryde (Quay Road) and Yarmouth (River Road) have a council car park on the oversize list; East Cowes and Fishbourne have none, so a large vehicle off a late Fishbourne or East Cowes crossing has nowhere designated to go. And the whole of the west and the far south - Freshwater Bay, Totland, Colwell, The Needles, Compton, Brook - is absent from the oversize list entirely; the only entry on that coast is Whale Chine at Chale, which is free with a 24-hour maximum and no facilities of any kind. The much-used informal spots on that side of the island (Culver Down, Fort Victoria, the radar station above Ventnor) are not council pay and display and are governed by whoever owns them, not by the parking order.

PROVISION THE PARKING PAGES DO NOT MENTION - CHECKED, NONE FOUND (27 July 2026). The council's parks, countryside, leisure, harbour and tourism pages were searched separately from the parking pages, along with 'Isle of Wight Council caravan park' and 'Isle of Wight Council campsite' generally. The unitary runs no campsite, caravan park, touring site or holiday park anywhere, leased or otherwise.

The eighteen parks the council manages directly - Princes Green, East Cowes Esplanade, Lake Cliff Gardens, Church Litten, Medina Arboretum, Seaclose, Appley Park, Ryde Seafront, Battery Gardens, Ferncliff, Sandham Grounds, Pier Gardens, Puckpool, Rylstone, Tower Cottage Gardens, The Cascades, Ventnor Park and Fort Victoria - are day-use gardens, esplanades and recreation grounds. None is designated a country park and none offers overnight stays. The Island's country parks and countryside sites, including Golden Hill and Pan, are looked after by the Gift to Nature charity rather than by council staff, following the council's 2015 decision to lease out its countryside estate; none of the Gift to Nature sites offers camping, caravanning or any overnight stay either. The council is the harbour authority for Newport, Ryde and Ventnor and publishes no overnight vehicle provision at any of the three. The Island's very large touring supply - Appuldurcombe Gardens, Nodes Point, Thorness Bay, Whitecliff Bay and the rest - is private or club-owned and should not be recorded under this authority; the council's only role there is licensing caravan and camping sites under the 1960 Act, which is regulation and not provision.

That matters for reading the file above. The Isle of Wight's answer to the motorhome is entirely a parking answer - a GBP2 overnight ticket in seventeen named car parks and on-street bays. There is no second, non-parking channel here of the kind Hampshire has at Calshot or the South Downs Authority has at Foxhole. What is on the parking pages is the whole of it.
open_questions: The full text of the Isle of Wight Council (Parking Places) (Consolidation) Order No 3 2023 and Order No 4 2023 could not be read - the Traffic Penalty Tribunal PDF repository is disallowed by robots.txt. The 'no cooking, sleeping, sanitary' clause is quoted from the council's own guidance page, not from the sealed order, so the article number and exact wording are unverified.

Does any prohibition on sleeping in a vehicle exist for ON-STREET bays? None was found, and the council sells a GBP2 overnight on-street ticket. If the answer is no, the island's on-street bays are more permissive overnight than its car parks.

What the Clearways Order No 1 2024 and the Prohibition of Parking on Verge or Footway Order No 1 2024 cover - both are listed as current on the tribunal repository but could not be read. Military Road viewpoints and Culver Down are the places where a clearway would matter to a van.
Is Whale Chine free, or is a tariff simply not shown? The motorhome page gives '24 hours max' in the cost column, which reads as a free 24-hour maximum stay but is not stated as such.

Shanklin Spa and Vernon Meadow are published with the same postcode (PO37 6BQ, now a terminated postcode), so both pins sit on the same centroid and neither is reliable. Ryde Quay Road (PO33 2HH) is also a terminated postcode. All seventeen pins are postcode centroids and none has been checked against imagery.
Whether the GBP2 overnight charge is standalone or must be bought on top of a day tariff that has already expired at 6pm - the tariff tables list it as a separate line but do not say.
Whether Fort Victoria Country Park, Culver Down and the other informally used spots are council land subject to the same parking order, or National Trust / other ownership with their own rules.
Whether any private aire or paid stopover operates on the island. Only conventional campsites and one pub stopover were found; no aire-format provision was identified.

sites.name: All Isle of Wight Council car parks (no cooking, sleeping or sanitary use of a vehicle)
sites.notes:
The single island-wide prohibition, and it is a ban on the ACT, not on the vehicle class. The council's own motorhome and oversize vehicle parking page states it flatly: 'You must not use your vehicle for cooking, sleeping, sanitary or any other purpose whilst in the car park.' No motorhome, campervan or motor caravan is excluded from any council car park anywhere on the island by class, and none of the seventeen sites the council lists for oversize vehicles has a height barrier. What is prohibited is living in the vehicle once it is parked.

The practical enforcement hook is not the sleeping clause but the bay rule that sits beside it: 'the whole of the vehicle must be inside the marked bay. If there is not a bay big enough, please find an alternative car park.' That is observable from outside the vehicle and generates a PCN; sleeping is not. Van users on forums report tickets for overhang, not for sleeping.

sites.name: All Isle of Wight Council off-street pay and display car parks (overnight parking permitted, GBP2 6pm-8am)
sites.notes:
The island prices the night rather than banning it. Every long-stay and short-stay council off-street tariff checked - Ryde, Cowes and East Cowes, Sandown, Ventnor, and the Colwell/Freshwater/Totland/Yarmouth group - carries the same line: 'overnight charge (6pm - 8am) - GBP2.00'. That is a published, purchasable right to leave a vehicle in a council car park all night, sold through PayByPhone or the machine, at a flat rate that does not vary by town or by vehicle size. The charge was introduced at GBP1 in 2019 and has since doubled.

Parking overnight is therefore lawful and cheap. Sleeping in the vehicle while parked is not lawful. A van user has to hold both facts at once.

sites.name: All Isle of Wight Council on-street pay and display bays (overnight parking permitted, GBP2 6pm-10am)
sites.notes:
Because the Isle of Wight is unitary it owns the highway as well as the car parks, and it has extended the same GBP2 overnight charge to its on-street bays - with a longer window, 6pm to 10am rather than 6pm to 8am. The seafront on-street runs are the ones that matter: Ryde Esplanade, Canoe Lake Road and North Walk in Ryde; Cowes Parade and Queens Road Esplanade; Ventnor Esplanade; Yarmouth Common and High Street.

No on-street order was found that bans motor caravans, restricts a bay to cars and motorcycles, or imposes a no-overnight-parking window - the manoeuvre that BCP, North Yorkshire and East Suffolk have all reached for. The off-street 'no sleeping' clause is a condition of the car park and does not obviously travel onto the highway, so the legal position of a van parked in a paid on-street bay overnight is materially better here than in a council car park. That gap has not been tested and the council has not commented on it.
